title: Unboxing Shein’s Hong Kong IPO - The Wire China
gist: Shein's Hong Kong IPO prospectus shows revenue growth halving to 8 percent in 2025 while fulfillment costs exploded by $6 billion between 2023 and 2025, driven by tariffs and the end of the U.S. de minimis exemption — with the EU's new 3-euro levy on low-value shipments set to repeat the damage in its other core market. The company is reportedly seeking a $40-50 billion valuation against a $98.2 billion peak in 2022, and withholds founder and insider ownership stakes in the prospectus.

themes.theme: Growth has stalled at the IPO

insights.claim: Shein's revenue grew 8 percent year-on-year in 2025, less than half the 19 percent annual growth rate it posted in 2024, with stagnation in the United States the main drag.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: A halving of growth into the listing undercuts the growth multiple the deal is being marketed on — price the IPO off decelerating, not compounding, revenue.
insights.quote: its overall revenue still grew by 8 percent year-on-year in 2025, but that was less than half the 19 percent annual growth rate in 2024
insights.locator: Two-thirds of Shein’s revenue now comes from the United States and Europe

insights.claim: E-commerce analyst Juozas Kaziukėnas reads the prospectus as showing that Shein has simply stopped growing, and that the equity story would have looked far more positive one or two years earlier.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: The listing looks like a late-cycle exit by existing holders rather than a growth financing — treat the timing itself as a signal.
insights.quote: The headline figure is that they have stopped growing,
insights.locator: “The headline figure is that they have stopped growing,”

insights.claim: Two-thirds of Shein's revenue now comes from the United States and Europe, concentrating the business in exactly the two jurisdictions imposing new levies on low-value cross-border parcels.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: Revenue concentration and regulatory exposure coincide — there is no geographic hedge inside the current revenue base.
insights.locator: Two-thirds of Shein’s revenue now comes from the United States

themes.theme: Tariff and de minimis cost shock

insights.claim: Nearly half of Shein's expenses in the first quarter of 2026 went to fulfilling customer orders, and its annual fulfillment costs rose by $6 billion between 2023 and 2025.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: A $6bn structural cost increase against single-digit revenue growth is the core margin problem — fulfillment, not marketing or product, is what breaks the model.
insights.quote: Its annual ‘fulfillment costs’ rose by $6 billion between 2023 and 2025.
insights.locator: Alongside slowing revenue growth, Shein has seen its costs rise

insights.claim: The U.S. government's 2025 decision to end the de minimis exemption from tariffs for low-value packages, alongside higher tariffs generally, is the main driver of Shein's cost increase, and the EU began implementing a 3-euro sales tax on low-value shipments from July 1.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: The regulatory arbitrage that built the direct-from-China parcel model is being closed in both core markets within roughly a year — a repeatable template for other cross-border retailers.
insights.locator: Higher tariffs and the U.S. government’s 2025 decision

insights.claim: Market conditions are becoming increasingly hostile for all direct-from-China retailers, with the golden age of that market opportunity now several years past and growth outside heavily taxed jurisdictions the remaining 'saving grace'.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: Read across to the whole direct-from-China parcel cohort; the residual growth case rests on lower-income, lightly taxed markets with weaker unit economics.
insights.quote: The golden age of the market opportunity was a few years back, and now market conditions are becoming increasingly hostile for all these kinds of direct-from-China retailers,
insights.locator: Shein could still grow in the rest of the world

insights.claim: Despite efforts to diversify supply chains and host third-party sellers on its marketplace, the bulk of Shein's products still ship from Chinese warehouses.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: The China-origin exposure that triggers tariffs and political scrutiny has not actually been reduced — diversification is presentational so far.
insights.locator: Despite Shein’s efforts to diversify its supply chains

insights.claim: Shein's private valuation has fallen from $98.2 billion in a 2022 Series D to $64 billion in the 2023 D+ round, and slowing growth suggests it may struggle to achieve even the $40-50 billion valuation reported for its Hong Kong IPO.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: A roughly 50-60 percent markdown from the 2022 peak is the benchmark for how far late-stage consumer-internet marks still have to travel to reach public clearing prices.
insights.quote: the company’s valuation has been in decline since it was valued at nearly $100 billion in a 2022 funding round
insights.locator: Shein’s slowing growth suggests it could struggle

insights.claim: Shein has been pushed down the listing-venue ladder by politics: U.S. scrutiny of its China ties derailed a 2023 New York Stock Exchange attempt, Chinese regulators quashed a later London listing, and Trump's trade war hit the business.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: Hong Kong is the residual venue for China-linked consumer platforms blocked in New York and London — expect more such listings and a structurally lower valuation for them.
insights.locator: But U.S. officials have also scrutinized the company

insights.claim: The prospectus withholds the size of founder Sky Xu's stake in SHEIN Global Holdings along with the shares held by the three other founding members and other investors, while Xu's Forbes-estimated net worth fell to $5.95 billion in 2025 from an $11 billion peak in 2024.
insights.speaker: The Wire China
insights.so_what: Undisclosed insider ownership in an IPO prospectus is a governance red flag that limits any assessment of control and lock-up overhang.
insights.quote: The size of his ownership in SHEIN Global Holdings is withheld in the prospectus, along with the share held by the other three founding members and other investors.
insights.locator: The size of his ownership in SHEIN Global Holdings
